# Review guide: vllm-torchtpu

Rule IDs (R-x.y, PR-x, P-x, Q-x) refer to `docs/developers_guide/{coding_guidance,optimization_best_practices}.md`.

## 1. How to review

Read the description, the diff, and each changed file with its callers. Apply every section 3 pass and each section 4 area whose glob matches a changed file. Never stop early: a missing eval does not replace checking for crashes and wrong output.

Anchor each finding on a line the PR adds or changes. For an untouched file (a missed sibling, a stale doc), use the changed line that causes it and name the file; for missing evidence, the line that needs it (a new kernel path with no eval); for removed code, the nearest added line in that file, quoting it. Only title or description problems (an overclaiming title, an internal link), and removed code in a file with no added line, go in the summary: 1 or 2 sentences, cut at 1,000 characters, most severe first.

Order findings blocking first, then should-fix, most severe first within each. Before output, drop findings that section 5 or a fine clause in any rule covers.

## 2. How to comment

- Put the label in the label field, not the text: `blocking` (wrong output, crash, hang, leaked secret, or a large serving slowdown, such as a per-step weight copy or a compile while serving), or `should-fix`. Findings are the only inline comments. A failure you can name but not confirm goes under questions, and minor polish under nits; both appear in the review summary. [B] and [S] give a rule's usual label and [N] marks a nit; label each finding by its own impact. "Ask" in a rule is a request the author should address and keeps the rule's label; "ask, do not block" means a question.
- One issue per comment, on the exact line, under 1,500 characters. A second finding on one line is dropped.
- You can read only this repo: the base branch at `./` (sometimes the PR's merge base) and the PR head at `./pr`. Raise upstream or newer-main mismatches only as a question saying what to check; never cite upstream files you did not read.
- **Concrete failures**. For a bug, give the inputs, config, and steps that break it; otherwise name the code and the fix. Do not flag a design only for differing from another approach. Do not claim a rewrite is faster or advise to "hint XLA"; ask for a timing, trace, or HLO dump.
- **Skip what tools enforce**. Ruff (including torch, torch_tpu, and vllm imports in `kernels/`), pyrefly, shellcheck, license headers (never suggest `SPDX-License-Identifier`; `SPDX-FileCopyrightText` lines are allowed), DCO sign-off, `os.getenv`, `os.environ.get`, and `os.environ[...]` reads under `src/vllm_torchtpu/` outside `envs.py` and `env_override.py`, what the `no-internal-refs` hook and PR Text check catch (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.github/workflows/pr-text.yml`; look for what they miss), and a `pallas.jax_op` file missing from `_RUNTIME_CACHE_KEY_PATHS`.
- **Names and links**. Cite rule IDs. Write people's names as plain text, not @-mentions. Never repeat an internal link; point to its line.

## 3. Repo-wide rules

### Pass 0: triage

- [B] **Internal references** (R-7.12). Flag anything outside readers cannot open, including in PR text: internal hosts, private repos, private container images or package indexes, internal job IDs or doc codes, private tracker tags, personal buckets. Public issues and plain-text private project names are fine. `.buildkite/`, `docker/`, and CI-only scripts may name the CI project `cloud-ullm-inference-ci-cd`, its registries, and `gs://tpu-commons-ci`; user-facing docs, examples, and scripts may not.
- [B] **Eval for output changes** (R-8.10, Q-3). Changes that can alter model output (new, swapped, or newly admitted kernels, quantized compute, collective or LSE (log-sum-exp) merge rewrites, scheduler chunking (run with the limit firing), new parallel layouts) need a before/after eval with commands, on one image at production parallelism for each enabled configuration, plus MTP acceptance length for models served with MTP. Ask about scores below the baselines in `scripts/vllm/benchmarking/baselines/eval/`. Smoke prompts and fake-sublayer tests do not count. Without an eval, the path ships default off or as bring-up only. A bit-exact test, identical greedy output, or, for a drafter-only change, unchanged acceptance length makes it unnecessary (section 5).
- [B] **Merge readiness** (R-7.6). If the description admits wrong output, ask for Draft. Ask for a rebase only when the diff or description shows staleness changes the result: the diff re-adds removed code, calls a renamed API, or relies on upstream code a newer pin changed. Never flag CI status alone.
- [B] **Fix has a failing test** (R-8.2). A bug fix in code a test can run (Python under `src/` or `tools/`, scripts `tests/scripts/` covers) needs a test that fails when the fix is reverted; other CI, Docker, and docs fixes need no new test. Tests that patch the fixed function, or use only inputs where old and new code agree, do not count.
- [S] **One purpose** (R-7.1, R-7.2, R-7.3, R-7.9). Ask about hunks the stated purpose does not need (drop a lone typo fix). Unless R-7.1's carve-outs apply, split distinct purposes (such as an enabling refactor plus a behavior change, R-7.2) at any size, and for single-purpose diffs well above R-7.1's 300-line soft target ask to split independently testable, measurable, or revertible steps; separate commits do not count, and raise any split request as an inline finding on the separable part's entry point. Shared-code changes in a model PR land first; the PR's own `_RUNTIME_CACHE_KEY_PATHS` entries belong in it. Each stacked PR runs without later PRs (flag code that needs an API only a later PR adds), links the others by number, and is retargeted to main after its base merges.
- [S] **Perf claims** (P-1, P-4, PR-1). A speedup needs same-rig before/after numbers (profiler off) on the same base and pins for each mode touched (prefill, decode, mixed), with commands, an xprof trace from a separate run, and the mechanism. Separable parts show separate gains. Gains within run-to-run spread are unproven. A changed config with a baseline updates it from a linked run. Make it a nit when speed is secondary.
- [S] **PR text** (R-7.11, PR-4, Q-6). Ask only for what applies, never for template headings alone: a fix gives the bug, symptom, and mechanism; a feature or knob says how to turn it on and off; weight-loading or model-level changes give before/after HBM and load time; a new model names its checkpoint and serve command. Limitations lists every added `NotImplementedError`, fallback, TODO, or gate. The title names the capability, not the model that prompted it, unless the change is model-specific (`[Model]` PRs name the model, per the template); title mismatches are nits. All text matches the PR head. Comments, docstrings, test names, errors, and env-var help claim only what the code does: TPU-only claims need a device check, tests assert what their names say, stated guarantees are enforced, and speed or accuracy claims need numbers (P-1, R-8.10).
- [S] **Tests for changed code** (R-8.1, R-8.4, R-8.5). Tests run the changed lines: new helpers, error paths, flag-on branches (the pytest lanes set no `TPU_*` flags), and every mode sharing the code. Prefer one parametrized test on the smallest hardware that runs the code (CPU, or `tpu_test` for Pallas kernels). If only nightly, perf-lane, or manual runs cover the change, ask for a per-PR test or a linked build. Compiled-path claims run under `torch.compile(backend="eager", fullgraph=True)`, upstream-behavior claims run real upstream code, and engine-only behavior can extend a `scripts/vllm/integration/` script. Code relying on memory never being read (pages dropped on a prefix-cache hit) needs a garbage-fill test with bit-identical output.

### Pass 1: intent and design

- [B] **Default off until validated** (R-6.2, R-4.4). A perf change altering defaults on configs the PR did not measure (global XLA or libtpu flags, a default tile) stays opt-in, or gated to the measured generation, until A/B data covers another generation and each existing model whose path or tile changes, with prefill, decode, and mixed numbers (PR-1). Gate by chip version (`pltpu.get_tpu_info()` in a TPU worker, `tpu_info.get_chip_version()` elsewhere); only `env_override.py` and `tpu_info.py` parse the accelerator-type string. User-visible differences from stock vLLM (served output, tokenization, failure handling), and behavior validated on some models only, sit behind a default-off `envs.py` flag whose installer returns early when off. Required TPU patches need no flag.
- [S] **Reuse first** (R-3.1, R-3.3, R-7.8). Search main and upstream vLLM for code that does the job, and name the file. Common misses: `_get_padded_token_len` (`runner/tpu_runner.py`), `synchronize_tensors` and `largest_divisor` (`utils.py`), `quantize_block` (`kernels/quantized_matmul/util.py`). Move a helper the caller must not import (R-2.1) to a shared home; new code goes where its concept lives, and `pallas_call` kernels under `kernels/`. Ask how a named overlapping PR differs.
- [S] **Extension points** (R-3.4, R-3.5). Prefer extension points over monkeypatches, and never set torch globals or upstream attributes process-wide for one call path. Patches wrap the original; a copied upstream body needs a reason and a comment naming its source and version. Test patches on the real upstream class. Workaround TODOs give the root cause, removal condition, and any public upstream link.
- [S] **New knobs** (R-6.1, R-6.2). For a new env var or flag, look for an existing vLLM or `envs.py` setting, and ask which R-6.2 case fits and who sets it. An exact-result speedup measured everywhere it applies becomes the default, without a flag. Accept a default-off flag (R-6.2 case a) whose description says why it is off or what data turns it on, and ask only when the flag goes; otherwise ask why (a question). A new threshold env var is itself a finding: ask for a cost-model value or tuned-table entry (P-15, P-16). A threshold that stays must hold its path in the phase it was built for (prefill or decode) after padding; a per-step threshold's comment says it compares with the padded `compile_sizes` bucket.
- [S] **Knob hygiene**. Knobs use a typed `envs.py` builder, a `TPU_` or `VLLM_TPU_` prefix, a unit in the name or comment, and a comment on values; a required knob gets no invented default. Defaults apply only to unset or `"auto"` values: an explicit value that cannot work raises, and an override warns. Removed options still set raise `ValueError` naming the replacement. Serving knobs get a row in `docs/reference/env_vars.md` (ask, do not block).
- [S] **Live callers** (R-7.5). New kernels, helpers, and parameters need a production caller in the PR (one behind a default-off selector counts), or a named follow-up for a kernel-only or refactor-first PR. Search string references (`patch_registry.py` targets, `pyproject.toml` entry points, `importlib`) before calling code unreached. Delete replaced mechanisms and aliases in the same PR, except superseded kernel versions (PR-3) and migration selectors (R-6.2).
- [S] **One source per fact** (R-3.3, R-4.2). Flag a second hand-written copy of a value, list, or gate another module owns, and name the helper (such as `static_verify_q_len(vllm_config)` or the kernel's `get_kv_cache_shape`). Each shared value has one writer; decide a mode or layout once per path. Deriving from argument shapes, and per-module copies of small pure helpers like `get_dtype_packing`, are fine.
- [S] **Key on the property** (R-2.2, R-6.5, R-6.6). Shared code keys on the property that drives the behavior, not model names, one setup's literals (`tokens == 8192`), or one model's constants. Model values such as a clamp limit come from the model config; shared code that supports one value for now raises `NotImplementedError` for others. Tuned-table keys on per-rank shapes (P-16), literals stating a kernel's envelope (P-17), and one helper for a truly unique model layout are fine.
- [S] **Derived constants** (R-4.4, R-4.5). Code that may run where no worker owns the TPU (shape helpers, connectors, scheduler code) uses `pltpu.get_tpu_info_for_chip` with a chip version, never `pltpu.get_tpu_info()`, which claims the TPU so later workers crash with EBUSY (device busy) (blocking; the rest is should-fix). New code uses a shared axis-name constant, not `P(None, "model")`. Other non-obvious numbers get a name or a comment; tuned tables and small obvious numbers are fine.

### Pass 2: correctness

- [B] **Unsupported combinations raise** (R-5.3, R-5.4). Reject unsupported options, layouts, and TPU generations where the config is first known (`check_and_update_config`, layer construction, or `validate_request`; weight processing for checks that need checkpoint tensors), never with an `assert` on a user setting. In `fullgraph` code such as the model forward, checks use `torch._assert(cond, msg)`. A tighter gate still accepts the configs in `examples/` and `.buildkite/`; a looser one tests each new combination.
- [B] **Siblings and callers**. A new option, hook, or fix reaches every sibling: early returns, fast paths, each KV connector, `OmniTpuPlatform`, each KV cache type, near-identical scripts. Interface changes update every caller and env-var reader, and the default config still starts with and without DCP. A change to what the unified pool stores updates every consumer (`gdn_pool_layout.py`, each `get_state_dtype()`, `kda_attention_op.py`, `tpu_block_size_utils.py`, `kv_cache_spec_normalizer.py`, and Raiden's `pool_manifest.py` and `gdn_conv_layout` fingerprint string). When a parallel mode becomes conditional, checks and sizes keyed on its old global condition use the per-call one. Siblings ignoring an output-changing option raise; speed-only options may document the limit. A bug left in a sibling copy is should-fix.
- [B] **No silent fallback** (R-5.1, R-5.3). Raise when a check fails, a lookup finds nothing, or input does not parse, unless the fallback keeps output identical at a known speed cost and logs `warning_once`, as a tuned-table miss logs its key (P-16). Flag new broad `except` blocks that return a default, pass, or only log; ask which input raises. Code that may run twice uses a once flag, not a swallowed error.
- [B] **Clear junk rows**. Clear padded or unrouted rows with `jnp.where(valid, x, 0)` before a matmul, permute, or reduction mixes them with real rows; a zero weight fails, since 0 * NaN = NaN. Prefer one select where rows mix. A select in an attention kernel's per-block loop needs microbenchmarks; a measurable cost goes behind a static config (`mask_invalid_v`).
- [B] **Trace-time values** (R-4.3). A compiled graph serves every batch padded to its size, so a Python branch taken while the graph is built (traced) may use only shapes, static args, and startup config, never batch contents. Pick kernels by batch composition with a device-side `jax.lax.cond` at the op level, never in a kernel's main loop (P-13), and accept padded metadata. Branch on token count only in the backbone; the MTP drafter (`eagle_head`) is traced once for all buckets, so ask how MTP is covered. Cached ops key on every baked-in value and never capture a layer's `self`.
- [B] **Match the upstream base** (R-3.1). TPU subclasses of vLLM classes keep the base signature at the pin, every keyword callers pass, inherited state, every handled path, and the exceptions callers catch (`KVCacheSpec.merge` raises `AssertionError`).
- [B] **Upstream at the pin** (R-2.5). Code relying on an upstream API, hook order, or behavior matches the version pinned in `pyproject.toml` (vLLM: the `vllm` group tag; vllm-omni: the `omni` extra). Never post "verified" notes. A pin bump removes the patches, registry entries, and shims it makes unneeded, here or in a follow-up.
- [B] **Moves keep behavior**. Code moved into a helper or `envs.py` keeps each caller's conditions, defaults, and handling of unset, empty, and zero values (`synchronize_tensors` waits by default; torch_tpu `sync.synchronize` does not). Comments lost in a move, and unexplained deleted blocks, are should-fix.
- [B] **Reaches the real path** (R-8.1). New code runs in every config that needs it: the layer is imported, branches match values the config really produces, setup hooks do not sit in functions some models skip, and attributes are set before every first read.
- [B] **Ports match the source** (PR-3). Ported code names its source and changes (should-fix if missing) and keeps the upstream copyright notice. It matches the source's math steps and overrides (flag a dropped `get_scheme` or an unneeded new override) and the GPU path's casts, rounding points, op order, and checks, with tests against the source per mode and dtype; a check dropped to avoid a device-to-host sync gets a comment. Describe private sources in words, never link them, and ask for clearance to publish.
- [B] **Changed numeric path** (Q-3, P-17). When existing shapes move to another numeric path, list every shape, dtype, and TPU generation it reaches; test each against the old path or exclude it in admission. The new path quantizes like the old one (scale blocks, activation quantize versus weight dequantize) unless the PR measures the difference.
- [B] **Exact admission** (R-5.2, P-17). Kernel wrappers, spec checks, and dispatch guards accept exactly what the kernel supports (rank, dtype, exact sizes, divisibility), name the bad value, and are never stricter than the kernel; a measured higher cutoff is fine (P-15). Keep asserts on invariants the kernel's indexing relies on.
- [B] **Custom op contracts**. `register_fake` returns the real op's shapes and dtypes for every input dtype. An op returning an updated cache donates it (should-fix if missing) and updates it in place (`.at[...].set`, `dynamic_update_slice`, an aliased Pallas output), not with `jnp.concatenate` or `jnp.pad`. Functions passed to `jax_op` take explicit, annotated parameters, not `*args`/`**kwargs` pass-through (R-4.7).
- [B] **KV cache dtype and layout**. Resolve `cache_dtype == "auto"` before shape math. With an fp8 KV cache, quantize only cached values, not attention queries, unless opt-in with an eval; the sparse-attention indexer's fp8 query is by design. Read the layout from `get_resolved_kv_cache_layout()`, not `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT`.
- [B] **Host buffers in flight**. Keep the CPU source of a `non_blocking=True` upload alive and unchanged until the copy ends (`stage_h2d_upload`, a staging tensor rewritten only after `_wait_input_staging_fence()`, or a blocking copy). Every path waits on a device-to-host copy's event before reading; a `None` event is fine only when no copy was issued.
- [S] **Concurrent writers**. When several processes or ranks can write one file, directory, or lock, name each writer by global rank or by every parallel axis running the code (an axis writing identical content may be left out, with a comment). Write-then-rename uses upstream `atomic_writer` (`vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils`) or a per-attempt temp name removed on failure. Locks key on the path they protect, or a value that maps one-to-one to it.
- [S] **No probing** (R-2.5, R-4.1, R-4.7). Flag new `getattr` defaults, `hasattr`, try-imports, class-name matching, and dispatch on repo-defined strings; suggest an enum, `isinstance`, or one named predicate, and, for an API the pin lacks, a pin bump (for vLLM, in an earlier upgrade PR, R-7.1). Defaults on Hugging Face config fields some checkpoints omit, compares with upstream string fields (`speculative_config.method == "mtp"`), and patch idempotence markers are fine.
- [S] **fp32 inside**. Inside a kernel or fused op, keep accumulators, scan carries, scale multiplies, divisions, normalizations, and activation functions (SiLU, sigmoid, softmax) in fp32, rounding to bf16 once at the store; matmul operands stay low precision (P-9). A commented bf16 round trip reproducing a reference rounding is fine. If a bf16 cast looks like a deliberate speed choice, ask its accuracy cost (P-3) instead of demanding fp32. For a bf16 collective or LSE merge sum (P-6), ask where it accumulates, for accuracy results, and for an fp32 switch (Q-4).

### Pass 3: TPU performance and memory

- [B] **Buckets and warmup**. Every reachable token or request count fits a precompiled bucket, including the draft forward and recompute after preemption; startup already rejects target budgets above the largest compile size (`_validate_token_budget_fits_compile_sizes`). Warmup compiles every bucket and path with serving's inputs, shapes, dtypes, and static args. When the PR adds a bucket, path, graph variant, or static arg, or changes compiled inputs, ask for a separate `VLLM_XLA_CHECK_RECOMPILATION=1` serving run with no new graphs after warmup.
- [B] **Per-step costs** (P-8, P-14). No per-step conversion, repacking, or padding of whole weights or caches (blocking; the rest is should-fix); pads past the native tile need a trace. Forward code avoids host round trips, or comments why. Derived-table caches hit every step, never keyed on a per-step view's identity. Flag a kernel call whose output is discarded (run only to write the KV cache), and a mask or zeroing pass the kernel can do itself unless a comment says why not. Small fused tensors and commented per-step casts (fp8 `W_UV` in `mla_attention_op.py`) are fine.
- [B] **Barriers need evidence** (P-13). A `lax.cond` added or moved on the per-layer path needs an end-to-end A/B on a full multi-layer model, with commands. An `optimization_barrier` needs proof (a failing numeric test, HLO, or a trace), a comment naming what it blocks, and scope limited to the inputs that need it.
- [B] **Compile cache key**. The key covers every input that changes a compiled program, and nothing else. Files building a `jax_op` sit under `_RUNTIME_CACHE_KEY_PATHS`; the guard test sees only the text `pallas.jax_op`, so check files importing `jax_op` from `torch_tpu._internal.pallas` by hand. Diffusion-only code in `_RUNTIME_CACHE_KEY_EXCLUDED_PATHS` is left out on purpose. Graph-neutral env vars go in `_TPU_COMPILE_ENV_IGNORED` with a reason; graph-affecting ones there are blocking. New cache directories key on `aot_compile_hash_factors` plus `compute_tpu_compilation_hash`.
- [B] **Sync scope**. Sync only the needed tensors (`wait=False` plus a `TpuEvent`), not the whole device, and never from a helper thread while the worker traces. Wait on prior-step results only where the host reads them. Assert tensor lists are non-empty; an empty list syncs nothing. A commented whole-device sync, such as a multi-chip pipeline hand-off, is fine.
- [S] **Prove layout claims** (P-2, P-9). Reshapes, transposes, or concats called free need HLO or a trace. Merging or splitting leading dims is a free bitcast; regrouping the last two dims usually copies the buffer, so allocate the regrouped layout up front. A speedup claimed from skipping a no-op pad or hand-merging collectives needs HLO showing XLA did not already do it; a plain `if pad > 0:` guard with no speed claim is fine. Matmul upcasts and `Precision.HIGHEST` need a commented reason.

### Pass 4: maintainability, tests, docs

- [B] **Env access** (R-2.6, `testing_and_ci.md`). Code under `src/vllm_torchtpu/` reads env vars only through `envs.py`, including forms the hook misses (`"X" in os.environ`, `from os import environ`, knob reads in `env_override.py`); kernels and jitted code get values from their wrapper. `tools/env_reads_baseline.txt` and `tools/b023_baseline.txt` (loop-variable closures in kernels) only shrink, though entries may move with a renamed file. `LIBTPU_INIT_ARGS` changes go through `env_override.py`. `BOOTSTRAP_VARS` names, and per-process bootstrap writes in platform, worker, and executor code, are fine; operator knobs never join that list.
- [B] **Patch registry** (R-3.5, `tpu_patch_mechanism.md`). Register each new patch in `patch_registry.PATCHES`, staged for every process that runs the patched code, before first use, with `refresh=` for by-name imports. Model patches set `model_config=True` and return `False` for other models; stage or order changes update `tests/platforms/test_patch_registry.py`. vLLM-Omni diffusion patches are the exception: one helper each in `omni/patches.py`. An idempotence guard covers only the swap, not the `refresh=` rebinding.
- [S] **Every line justified** (R-7.4, R-7.5). Delete code the PR adds or makes unreachable that cannot change behavior, unless a one-line comment says why it stays. Ask what each new guard prevents (call it dead only if its config is unsupported on main) and what each removed guard protected. Do not flag pyrefly narrowing (`assert x is not None`, `typing.cast`; `type_checking.md`), asserts on untested internal assumptions (R-5.2), or `NotImplementedError` for unsupported cases (R-5.3); an assert that alone checks a user setting falls under Unsupported combinations raise.
- [S] **Stale references**. Update every place still describing a changed behavior, name, pin, flag, or default, including untouched docs. Doc vLLM versions and the `vllm_test_utils` pin match the `vllm` pin. Ask only about text this PR makes stale; dated image tags and `support_matrices/verified_commit_hashes.csv` keep old versions on purpose.
- [S] **Log unexpected paths** (R-1.7). Overrides, fallbacks, skipped patches, and self-disabling optimizations log once (`info_once` or `warning_once` where the path can repeat) with the setting and values. A patch callback's one `Applied TPU patch: <what>` line may use plain `logger.info`, since the registry runs each callback once. No per-step INFO logs, and no module-level `_warn_once` helper.
- [S] **Names match behavior**. Names, labels, and trace fields say what the code does and keep their repo-wide meaning: name a collective by its real data movement, use `quant_dtype` for the logical dtype and `dtype` for storage, keep `TraceAnnotation` `num_reqs` unpadded. Unexplained abbreviations, booleans whose name reads like a value (such as `key_fp8`, but not clear flags such as `causal`), and two names for one concept are nits; single letters suit loop indices and math.
- [N] **Readable code** (R-1.1, R-1.8). Comments describe the code as it is, without change history, this repo's PR numbers, A/B results, or file:line references; provenance notes (PR-3), tuned-constant measurement notes, and upstream-fix TODOs (R-3.4) are fine. Flag undefined coined terms and "same contract as X" pointers (should-fix); standard vLLM and TPU terms need no definition. Kernel and re-layout docstrings state the data contract (packed axis, logical or physical shape, fused activation) and unexpected costs. Name non-obvious conditions, and put a TODO at each deferred fix. Imports go at module top except in patch callbacks, for optional extras, or with a comment naming the cycle.

## 4. Area rules

### Kernels: `src/vllm_torchtpu/{kernels,megakernel}/**`

- [B] **DMA bounds**. With `disable_bounds_checks=True`, every DMA stays inside live data: none for empty inputs or padded rows, sources clamped to the last live page, ring offsets wrapped, VMEM destinations in range at the largest loop index. The loop provably runs as many steps as the DMA prologue starts, and admission proves every whole DMA tile fits.
- [B] **TPU test per path** (R-8.1, R-8.4). Each new Pallas kernel, argument, mode, or dtype path needs a `tpu_test` running the real kernel against an independent NumPy or JAX reference; plain JAX helpers can test on CPU (R-8.5). Patched-out kernels and Python stand-ins for a Pallas `Ref` do not count. An untested kernel is blocking; a missing case for a new argument is should-fix.
- [B] **DMA slot reuse**. Never start a DMA into a slot before the last DMA on it is waited on; fix races with waits, semaphores, or more buffers, not timing. A guard that avoids such a race stays until a `pltpu.InterpretParams(detect_races=True)` test covers at least 3 grid steps with several rows per tile.
- [B] **VMEM and SMEM fit** (R-4.4, P-10). Tiles fit VMEM at the largest supported shape, counting double buffers and scratch. Tile budgets come from the chip's VMEM size with a margin (`pltpu.get_tpu_info()` in a worker, `pltpu.get_tpu_info_for_chip` in shape helpers); the compiler's `vmem_limit_bytes` may equal capacity. Flag an SMEM table only when its rows bypass the runner caps (`get_max_num_seqs_for_pages`, `num_reqs_max_model_len`) or grow with context; ask with its size at the longest context, and block only on overflow at a supported config.
- [B] **Self-contained kernels** (R-2.1, R-2.3, R-2.4). Kernels take settings as arguments, with no `envs` reads and no `layers` or `runner` imports. Reusable pieces stay out of model-named directories.
- [S] **Extend, do not fork** (R-3.2, R-6.3, PR-3). Push back on near-copy kernels and special-case stages; add an option to the existing one. A versioned successor that states when the old kernel goes is fine. For a kernel with a second home (`kernels/deepseek_v4/`, Tokamax's `streamindex_topk`), ask the author to confirm the other copy changes too; call a private one "the internal copy".
- [S] **Time tuned values** (P-15, P-16). Changes to block sizes, tiles, VMEM fractions, or admitted shapes need on-hardware timing on the current head per affected generation, including untargeted paths; only measured generations count as calibrated. Skip this when speed cannot change.
- [S] **DMA scheduling** (P-7, P-11). Wait on a DMA just before first use, and start independent copies first. Hoist loop-invariant weight or scale loads and casts, unless keeping them live spills vector registers; do not flag repeated pure math in a Python-unrolled loop, which the compiler usually merges. Avoid many tiny serial grid steps.

### Layers and quantization: `src/vllm_torchtpu/{layers,lora,models}/**`

- [B] **One MoE decision**. Every site that picks a layer's MoE path, or who runs its DP/PCP collectives, gives the same answer. Per-layer arming comes from what `prebuild_fused_moe_ep` stored on the layer's quant method (`fused_moe_ep_supported(qm)`), never the env flag; process-wide choices come from one shared predicate. Admission finishes before any requant or weight install. Test rank-summing ops at PCP > 1.
- [B] **Shared MoE entry points** (Q-1). Route through `moe_routing.route()` and resolve activations through `TpuMoEActivationMixin`. A fused kernel that routes inside refuses routing it cannot reproduce (a custom routing function, another scoring function, grouped top-k).
- [B] **Runner mesh**. The runner's JAX mesh holds one device per worker. A kernel builder (`pallas.jax_op(mesh=...)`) given the wrapper context's mesh takes it through `get_pallas_op_mesh()`; a test catches direct uses, so look for meshes saved on `self` or returned by helpers. World-sized meshes (PCP, EP), and a wrapper mesh bound into the kernel body, are fine. JAX-side TP branches on the runner mesh are dead code (should-fix).

### Models: `src/vllm_torchtpu/models/**`

- [B] **Declare only what works**. Declare only supported mixins and modality limits, and limit or reject at startup a capability that works only in some modes. Register every `architectures` name of the released checkpoint (also in `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` if the model has TPU config checks), or state that the checkpoint does not run yet (should-fix). Load every key an accepted variant ships, or reject the variant at config time.

### Runner and worker: `src/vllm_torchtpu/{runner,worker,core,executors,structured_decoding,spec_decode}/**`, `src/vllm_torchtpu/kv_cache_*.py`

- [B] **Async placeholders**. Under async scheduling, `output_token_ids` holds `1 + num_draft` placeholders until `_modify_prev_results` runs; do not count or read them before. A layout that reorders tokens maps request-major order to local positions (`local_index_for_request_major_token`).
- [B] **Idempotent helpers**. A helper that runs twice must not build on env values it exported, or reset state whose inputs did not change.
- [B] **Batch indexing**. Slice batch-wide per-request data to each chunk with `[start_index:end_index]`, but never offset buffers `_prepare_inputs` rebuilds per chunk (`query_start_loc_np`, `positions_np`, `input_ids_cpu`). After `_reorder_batch_for_rpa`, find rows via `req_id_to_index`. Bound loops over real request counts by `max_num_seqs`; loops over the padded buckets in `num_reqs_paddings` may use `max_num_reqs`.
- [B] **Pipeline stages**. Per-step logic handles non-last PP stages, where `hidden_states` is `IntermediateTensors` (do not assume its keys) and the step returns early; state needed later travels with `_pp_pending_scheduler_output`.
- [B] **KV cache setup**. Loops over `group.layer_names` skip `shared_kv_cache_layers` (a nit in DeepSeek-V4-only code). Allocation changes keep `check_kv_caches_cover_block_ids` running before binding. It skips block-major, DeepSeek-V4, MLA, and unified-pool caches on purpose.
- [S] **Per-step host work**. Allocate per-step buffers once at padded shapes and fill them in place; create device constants once. Avoid per-token Python loops (loops over requests, and tensors created inside compiled code, are fine). `non_blocking=True` upload sources follow Host buffers in flight.
- [S] **Memory accounting** (Q-6). HBM held while serving exists before `determine_available_memory()` profiles, or is subtracted from the KV budget (`estimate_kv_connector_hbm_reserve`). One-off warmups go in `capture_model()`, not `load_model()`; compiles in `profile_run()` are intentional.
- [S] **Runner test stand-ins** (R-8.7). When a runner change adds an attribute or moves where a value is computed, every `SimpleNamespace` or `MagicMock` runner stand-in sets it, and overrides of the old setup point move to the new one.

### Distributed: `src/vllm_torchtpu/distributed/**`, `src/vllm_torchtpu/layers/adapter/*moe*.py`

- [B] **Mesh order**. An EP mesh index is not the EP rank: map with `ep_rank_order()` and `ep_mesh_index()`, and keep order choices in `_ep_mesh_order`. Device-order changes match every mesh in the compiled module; test PCP > 1 and DCP > 1. A per-rank check that decides whether a collective kernel runs gives the same answer on every rank, or raises.
- [S] **New transfer layouts**. A PR enabling a KV transfer or multi-host layout (TP to DP, DP4TP2) shows an end-to-end run per new layout and updates both the admission topology and the resharding plan for every direction.

### Speculative decoding: `src/vllm_torchtpu/{spec_decode,runner}/**`

- [B] **Lockstep replay**. Under EP-DP lockstep (`_dp_lockstep_sharded()`), idle ranks replay the draft step so every rank runs the same collectives. A new draft path must be off there at run time (blocking), and not built or precompiled (should-fix), unless the replay emits the same collectives.

### Omni: `src/vllm_torchtpu/omni/**`

- [B] **Orchestrator off the TPU**. Code that can run in the vLLM-Omni orchestrator never opens the TPU: no TPU tensors, TPU-backed generators, or memory queries through JAX or `torch.accelerator`. Never suggest `hbm_usage_bytes()` or `compute_hbm_budget()` there; HBM size comes from torch_tpu's `hardware.get_hbm_bytes_per_device()`. Move tensors to CPU before IPC.
- [B] **Worker setup**. `OmniTpuPlatform` reuses `TpuPlatform` methods. Read `WORLD_SIZE` only in `set_device`. Rebuild `TORCH_TPU_SLICEBUILDER_ADDRESSES` from the worker's own `MASTER_PORT`, never keep an inherited value, and raise for layouts known not to work.
- [S] **Patch scope**. Patch a shared class for every user, with a fallback to the original, unless measurements show it loses elsewhere; never gate it on a hand-copied list of pipeline names. A needed list gets a `tests_omni/` test against the real vllm-omni registry in both directions, and an INFO log when no model patch applies.

### KV offload and transfer: `src/vllm_torchtpu/{offload,distributed/kv_transfer}/**`

- [B] **Report failures**. Report failed loads per request through `get_transfer_results()` (`failed_recving`) on every connector, not only as block IDs; unsupported user-reachable hooks warn and return False. By default a failed load fails the request; do not claim it recomputes.
- [B] **Raiden layouts**. Raiden copies raw bytes between peers, so the layout fingerprint changes with any byte-layout change and omits values peers may differ in, such as head sharding. Attention KV block-id and capacity math uses `block_size * max(pcp, dcp)`; one rank's physical page uses plain `block_size`; GDN/Mamba state scales by PCP only.
- [B] **Clear stashed state**. State a scheduler hook saves for a later hook (such as `lookup()` for `prepare_load()`) is also removed when the later hook never runs: an aborted, preempted, or skipped request. Drop per-step leftovers in `on_schedule_end()` or `build_connector_meta()`, or per-request entries in `on_request_finished()`.

### Tests: `{tests,tests_omni}/**`

- [B] **Test the real path** (R-8.1, R-8.7). Tests run the production code they name in its real configuration: no patched function under test, inputs that reach the branch, real configs where code reads derived values. Prove gated, fused, or quantized paths ran (a gate assert, a spy, or a finite SNR). Mocks for parts that do not decide the result, and `__new__` construction unless the skipped `__init__` matters, are fine.
- [B] **Markers and lanes** (R-8.4). Unmarked tests run on CPU, `tpu_test` on one chip (2 devices), `multichip` beyond that; `nightly` keeps its hardware marker. vllm-omni tests go in `tests_omni/` with `omni`. Every file in `tests/` imports on the CPU agent. A device-count skip that always fires on the test's own lane is blocking. If a PR adds a model load, full checkpoint, or long parity run to a per-PR lane without stating its runtime, ask (a question); small-model smoke tests are fine on every PR, and `nightly` suits long runs only if a per-PR test still covers the change.
- [B] **Asserts that can fail** (R-8.2). Tolerances come from measured error or format precision, so an all-zero output fails. References never reuse the code under test; parity tests build CPU references from CPU inputs. Shape or dtype asserts suit a shape contract (a `register_fake` test), and smoke tests suit paths another test checks for values. Loose tolerances and proxy-only checks are should-fix; self-referencing checks and asserts that cannot fail are blocking. Tests of masks, bitmasks, filters, and golden thresholds need a must-fail control: the check fails on known-wrong output (perturb the TPU output, not the reference). Leave unchanged tolerances alone, and add no timing asserts (R-8.9).
- [S] **Boundary inputs** (R-8.3). Inputs reach the edges the change handles: partial last blocks, multi-block sequences, uneven splits, non-zero offsets, mixed batches, padded slots. Ask only for cases that reach changed code, as parameters of one test. When code requires aligned input because the runner pads (P-14), ask for an assert on that contract (R-5.2) instead.
- [S] **Test isolation**. Restore process-wide state with `monkeypatch`. No import-time `jax.config`, `os.environ`, or `sys.modules` changes; stub modules only inside a test with `monkeypatch.setitem`. Session-wide `os.environ.setdefault` in `tests/conftest.py`, and env writes in a spawned child process, are fine.
- [S] **Extend existing tests** (R-8.3, R-8.8). Reuse existing tests, shared helpers, and gold references. Name new test files by mechanism, not model, unless they test model-specific code (R-2.4). Flag deleted asserts unless the behavior they covered is gone. Import required packages at module top; `pytest.importorskip` is for optional extras.

### CI and build: `{.buildkite,docker,scripts,tools,.github,examples,requirements}/**`, `pyproject.toml`

- [B] **Fail on missing inputs**. Scripts exit non-zero, naming the missing input. No `|| true` on a fetch unless an empty check follows at once, and no fallback to `:latest`, vLLM HEAD (allowed only in the integration branch of `.buildkite/scripts/bootstrap.sh`), synthetic data, or zero metrics; jobs testing a newer version never fall back to the pin. Cleanup `|| true`, and `docker/build_image.sh` defaulting to the pin, are fine.
- [B] **CI variables** (R-7.4). Every pipeline that runs a shared script sets its new inputs, and pod-read vars join `FORWARD` in `.buildkite/kubernetes/common.sh` (`BUILDKITE_*` and agent-only names need no entry). Each shell value has one definition, and later steps read the meta-data an earlier step stored. Grep each new env var, flag, and step setting for a reader, including keys built from variables (`CI_IMAGE_TAG${IMAGE_SUFFIX:-}`) or read by generic getters; dead ones are should-fix.
- [B] **Publish and release**. Docker Hub and PyPI pushes run only for `main` nightlies or approved `releases/vX.Y.Z` builds, and publishing secrets stay out of the PR pipeline. Side-effect steps run after the steps proving them safe, with every `depends_on` key defined in an uploaded lane. A check replacing a human approval rule (code-owner review) comes from a dedicated GitHub App that no label passes, or the native rule stays; ordinary checks are exempt. Release scripts use their own checkout's tooling, match branches with `RELEASE_BRANCH_REGEX` (never `releases/*`), log in only through `dockerhub_login`, and commit or push only from a trap-removed `git worktree` with per-command identity (should-fix).
- [B] **Shell scripts**. Read the script's `set` line. Under `set -u`, check moved assignments; under `set -e`, handle expected failures with `||`. `set -e` is off inside `$(...)`, so end failing commands there with `|| die` or `|| exit 1`. Scratch files go in `mktemp -d` paths a `trap ... EXIT` removes, not shared caches; a fixed `/tmp` path in a pod is fine. `rm -rf` on a variable uses `${VAR:?}`.
- [B] **Dockerfile**. Each stage redeclares the `ARG`s it reads. Keep `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty` and the base toolchain unless the PR says why, and keep `prod` last. Anchor `pyproject.toml` rewrites to the exact requirement, and redo them after each `COPY . .`.
- [B] **Pipeline YAML**. Use `$$` for run-time shell values. End continued lines with `\`, except lines ending in `&&`, `||`, or `|`, or inside a quoted `bash -c` string, and never comment out a middle line. Insert list items whole.
- [S] **Benchmark baselines** (PR-1). New steps add perf and eval baselines for every task. No shrunken workloads in perf-gated configs and no `soft_fail: true`; for unknown eval noise, set `EVAL_SOFT_FAIL` in the step or widen `EVAL_TOLERANCE`. Ask where new baseline numbers come from; scores far from the model card suggest a harness problem. Result metadata records every setting that changes the measurement. `check_regression.py` threshold changes keep missing-stderr and missing-key handling consistent across code, docs, and tests.
- [S] **CI steps can run** (R-8.4). Check that `bootstrap.sh` uploads a new or changed step and its `if:` can be true; a step that can never run silently drops its tests. Never ask for a build, a CI run, or a label to prove a step ran. Keep coverage: new configurations get new steps, one per-PR job keeps defaults, and nightly steps stay supersets of PR steps.
- [S] **No copied lanes**. Extend existing pipelines and scripts instead of copying them; per-model configs that only set values and source a shared base (such as `recipe-base.sh`) are the intended pattern. No host-specific paths. Large multihost checkpoints stream from `gs://` with `--load-format runai_streamer`; reuse `.buildkite/scripts/stage_model_snapshot.sh` instead of new copy logic.

### Docs: `docs/**`, `**/*.md`

- [S] **Commands that work**. For a doc command that does not copy a config in `scripts/vllm/benchmarking/configs/`, ask whether it was run on TPU; recipes nobody ran are labeled as examples. Image names match their target: `:nightly` has the test dependencies, `:latest` does not.

## 5. Do not flag

- **CI evidence and status**. Requests for a build link, a CI run, or a `run-full-ci` or `run-perf-eval` label to prove a step ran; CI status and failing jobs. CI must pass before a PR merges. Still flag a change that makes a test or step stop running at all.
- **Old problems**. Issues the PR did not create or worsen, such as style in moved code; mention them at most as a follow-up. Still flag an old bug the change starts to rely on or makes reachable.
- **Allowed patterns**. A narrow `except` where passing is provably safe; `try/finally` that only closes bookkeeping; a private-sentinel `getattr` that makes a patch install once.
- **Omni patterns**. Patches of private vLLM-Omni functions with a root-cause comment and a removal condition (ask for an upstream issue, not removal); commented `.cpu()` before IPC or CPU-built modules; per-worker env writes in `OmniTpuPlatform.set_device` before the first TPU allocation, except a raw `LIBTPU_INIT_ARGS` edit (use `set_libtpu_flag_default`).
- **Kernel idioms**. A rounding step whose comment names the reference path it reproduces; NaN in padded rows that nothing reduces over; a Python slice such as `x[:, k:k + 512]` on a short last block (not `pl.ds`); lane padding to 128 inside a kernel body; asserts on internal invariants.
- **Layout and dequant**. KV caches allocated in the kernel's tiled layout; `copy_` after a `jax_op` that donates the cache; dequantizing 4-bit weights with blocks smaller than the MXU column (mxfp4, int4 on gmm_v2) before the matmul, though a new hard-coded small requant target needs a reason (P-9).
- **Repo idioms**. The `torch_tpu._internal.pallas.jax_op` bridge; `synchronize_tensors` in warmup, precompile, and weight loading.
- **Test patterns**. Unmarked CPU tests; golden tests that compare with a stored reference by tolerance, not hash, unless the threshold passes broken output; module-top imports of packages the lane installs; a test's own independent reference.
- **CI patterns**. The paired (PR) and (Nightly) steps in `pipeline_tests.yml` and `pipeline_tests_cpu.yml`; YAML anchors that supply a step's commands; `|| true` in CI cleanup; the `torchtpu-vllm` compatibility names; the `vllm_test_utils` git dependency.
- **Requests for defensive code**. Asking for checks on inputs no caller passes, or `getattr` defaults on attributes the type guarantees; probes the PR adds still fall under No probing.
- **Deletions**. A disabled feature's lines deleted instead of commented out; a file deleted at one path and re-added at another.
- **Upstream and platform**. A TPU model definition under `models/vllm/` only because it exists; a `TpuPlatform` override of a vLLM Platform hook with no local caller, and its `model_config is not None` guards; `shard_map` with `check_vma=False`.
- **Spec decode and KV**. A drafter-only change with unchanged acceptance length and no accuracy eval (ask if it touches the target forward, the rejection sampler, the draft probabilities, or any KV, metadata, or buffer the target reads); a fence on the KV buffers before an offload or transfer reads HBM.
